articles.title_orig: What led Giants to their J.J. McCarthy decision: ‘Felt very strongly’
articles.title_zh: What led Giants to their J.J. McCarthy decision: ‘Felt very strongly’
articles.content_orig:
Desperate times sometimes call for desperate measures.
The Giants trading for J.J. McCarthy applies here.
Get texts from Paul Schwartz with all the latest Giants news and insights, exclusive to Sports+ subscribers.
In need of a backup quarterback, the Giants on Monday sent a 2027 fifth-round draft pick to the Vikings for McCarthy, who had been a colossal bust during his two-plus years in Minnesota. McCarthy joins a quarterback room devoid of Jaxson Dart — out for the season following knee surgery — and he will learn the playbook as Jameis Winston continues to start.
“Really glad, really happy, very excited to add J.J. McCarthy,” head coach John Harbaugh said. “I think he’s a strong young quarterback … very talented player and he’s gonna make us a stronger football team. I think it makes us better.”
Once Dart went down and out, the Giants knew they needed a better option behind Winston than Jake Haener, a 27-year-old with one NFL start. McCarthy has talent, but the Vikings being willing to give up on him so quickly after making him the No. 10 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft indicates how swiftly he fell out of favor with head coach Kevin O’Connell, who is known for his ability to work with and improve quarterbacks.
“He’s a talented guy,” Harbaugh said. “There’s just no doubt about it, he’s talented. He was a top 10 pick for a reason. I know he didn’t hold on to that job in Minnesota and that’s why he’s available.”
Haener was waived and will re-sign to the practice squad. The team will determine later in the week whether McCarthy or Haener serves as the backup to Winston for Sunday’s game against the Cardinals.
There is no change at starting quarterback.
“Jameis will be the starter for as long as I can see into the future but I don’t know,” Harbaugh said. “Nobody knows.
“I know that I have complete confidence that Jameis is going to play a great football game on Sunday and our guys are going to play great around him.”
McCarthy, 23, is four months older than Dart. He won a national championship at Michigan and went 27-1 as the starter, playing for Jim Harbaugh, John’s younger brother. John Harbaugh downplayed that connection, saying he paid special attention to Michigan while his brother was there and thus formed his own opinion of McCarthy. He said Jim “always had good things to say about J.J.”
The Giants scouted McCarthy heavily leading into the 2024 draft, as they certainly were in the quarterback market. Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels and Drake Maye went first, second and third to the Bears, Commanders and Patriots, respectively. The Giants owned the No. 6 overall pick and could have taken McCarthy but they passed on him and opted for wide receiver Malik Nabers.
It is believed the Giants had a second-round grade on McCarthy and they had reservations about his mental makeup and how he would fare playing in the fishbowl of the New York/New Jersey market.
Conversations about adding a quarterback started soon after Dart went down in the Week 2 loss to the Rams. Harbaugh said general manager Joe Schoen and the team’s “high-level scouts” brought McCarthy’s name to the table.
“They felt very strongly he was going to be a good option,” Harbaugh said. “That was interesting to me.
“He can throw it, he can run it, he makes plays. There’s a lot of things he can do better from what he did, obviously and we’re going to see where it goes from here.”
McCarthy missed his entire rookie season with a knee injury while backing up Sam Darnold. Despite going 14-3, the Vikings traded Darnold to the Seahawks and named McCarthy their starting quarterback. It turned out to be a huge miscalculation.
McCarthy won his NFL debut with a comeback victory over the Bears and was named the NFC Offensive Player of the Week. It went downhill rather rapidly from there. He missed five games with a high ankle sprain and one more with a fracture in his right hand. In 10 starts, he completed 57.4 percent of his passes, with 11 touchdown passes and 12 interceptions for a passer rating of 72.6. He went 6-4 as a starter and struggled mightily with ball placement and a general lack of maturity.
The Vikings signed Kyler Murray in free agency and McCarthy dropped so low on the depth chart that he was the No. 3 quarterback, behind Murray and Carson Wentz.
At 6-foot-3 and 219 pounds, the athletic McCarthy gives the Giants a much more mobile option. Winston, making his first start this season in place of Dart, played in the wind and rain this past Sunday and completed 14 of 22 passes for 118 yards, failing to get his team in the end zone in a 12-7 victory over the Titans.
At this point, there is no expectation that Winston’s hold on the starting job is in jeopardy. That could change, of course, based on the results and how quickly McCarthy picks up the offensive system.

articles.title_zh: Nothing’s New Headphone (1) Pro Are Made for the Studio
articles.content_orig:
The Headphone (1) Pro is Nothing's newest pair of cans, the company announced on Monday at an evening event in New York City. The headphones resemble Nothing’s first-ever over-ear headphones that debuted last summer , though the design and fit have been refined. The key change, though, is audio quality.
Instead of a single dynamic driver producing the sound in each earcup, Nothing has outfitted the Headphone (1) Pro with three drivers for each ear. Most headphones use a single 40-mm dynamic driver, so a single speaker ends up handling the bass, mids, and treble of your tracks. That can cause some muddiness and distortion. Adding more drivers—one for each specific frequency spectrum—gives the sound more room to stretch out and sparkle.
There’s a 40-mm bass dynamic driver to handle the low end. Then there’s a precision dynamic driver to tackle the midrange sounds like vocals, pianos, and guitars. The company says this driver will render those “S” and “T” sounds with more detail. Finally, there's the treble driver for the highs. Nothing’s driver uses xMEMS technology , which relies on a silicon diaphragm that should make transients—sharp bursts like a cymbal hit or a spiky synth stab—sound clearer.
All of these drivers working together should produce richer sound that’s more detailed overall. Every headphone maker claims their gadget produces the best sound on the market, but at least Nothing has attempted some technical feats here to try to convince you.
What's neat is you can see elements of the triple-driver architecture on the sides of the headphones—Nothing has added a couple of 9H Panda glass panels so you can peep the tech inside. The rest of the headphones are largely aluminum with titanium accents.
You'll no doubt worry about cracking that glass; Nothing claims that it is “shatter- and scratch-resistant," but Philipp Von Lintel, associate principal industrial designer at Nothing, says the glass had to survive durability tests 18 times from a drop of more than 1 meter. Also, the glass construction shouldn't affect repairability much—repair technicians can heat the glass from the outside to remove it and access the internal chamber for fixes. “Even if you crack it, there's a plastic film that keeps the chamber still working,” Von Lintel tells WIRED.
The Headphone (1) Pro is slightly lighter (by 2 grams) than the Headphone (1), with a wider headband and thicker padding, though battery life isn't as long, down to 68 hours with active noise canceling turned off versus 80. It has an IP52 dust- and water-resistance rating , so keep the hood of your rain jacket raised on rainy days.
Almost every gadget maker tosses the “Pro” moniker in the product name to justify a few extra features and a price bump. Yes, the Headphone (1) Pro cost $399, a $100 bump over the standard Headphone (1), but Nothing claims it is specifically catering to not just the average consumer who wants better sound, but also recording artists and audio professionals who work in the studio.
The company is including a feature that activates a flat equalization (EQ) mode—something mix engineers and audio producers prefer when they’re working—that’s triggered by a physical button on the headphones. Nothing collaborated with Metropolis Studio , a pro recording studio, to make the EQ features. There's even a “Studio B” Dynamic Spatial Audio mode that simulates Metropolis' mixing room, and four other Custom EQ profiles, like Concert Hall or Club. And yes, there’s a 3.5-mm jack so you can plug in (or stick with hi-res wireless or USB-C).
Charlie Smith, Nothing’s chief brand officer, says people will want these headphones for their commute to work. “That's fine, but people are making music on the go and need studio-level sound wherever they are," he says.
Nothing also claims the headphones have the best active noise cancellation it’s ever shipped, thanks to the use of 10 microphones to filter out ambient sounds. (Apple's AirPods Max , for comparison, use eight.)
“To us, this is a flagship product where we're able to showcase what we can do," Smith says. “It also helps elevate us as a brand.”
Sadly, they don’t fold up. Instead, Nothing is following Apple’s lead by including a bra-like carry case to keep the cans protected.
They'll officially hit store shelves on September 29—not only on Nothing's online store and Amazon, but also nationwide in Best Buy stores across North America.

articles.content_orig:
We still do not know what fate awaits Manchester City . The Citizens were found guilty of 114 of the 115 financial breaches of the Premier League's Financial Fair Play regulations, and the Sky Blues await their punishment.
And in England, statements attributed to Thierry Henry have been circulating on this subject. In these remarks, the former French international striker supposedly called for very heavy sanctions against City.
However, Henry said the statements were fabricated. In a post on his Instagram account, the former Gunner said he had never made such declarations. "Fake news. I haven't spoken to anyone from Manchester City. Stop making up stories."
This international break is anything but restful for Manchester City. On Friday, the English club was found guilty on almost all 115 Financial Fair Play counts.
The Athletic dropped the bombshell, and other media outlets later confirmed it. Afterward, Etihad Stadium residents shared their initial reactions in an interview with Sky Sports .
"The Premier League's proceedings are ongoing, with some important elements still to be finalized, and are subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC's position remains consistent with the statement the club issued in February 2023. The club has scrupulously adhered to the established procedure for the past eight years, based on the principle that the Premier League board and management would act as an independent, impartial, and fair regulatory authority, free from partisan influence."
This weekend, Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak published a letter to the fans, who are understandably very worried with this Damocles' sword hanging over the club.
"I have been part of this club for 18 years. I have had the privilege of being with you at the Etihad, Wembley, and Istanbul. This club means a lot to me, and you have shown me, time and time again, just how much Manchester City means to you. That is why I am writing to you today (…) Following the news reported by the media on Friday, many of you probably spent your evening answering questions and messages from friends, family, and colleagues. Me too. Here is what I told my family: the Premier League process still has a long way to go, and our confidence and determination to prove the club's innocence are just as strong as they were at the beginning of this matter."
Publicly, Manchester City are defending themselves fiercely and projecting a certain composure. But this announcement has not gone unnoticed. Besides other Premier League clubs looking to shed light on the affair and even demand sanctions, some others are considering taking advantage of City's potential misfortune to make moves.
The Sun explained this on Monday. The British publication, which consulted Spanish sources, indicates that Josko Gvardiol, Ayyoub Bouaddi , Elliot Anderson , Enzo Fernandez , and Rayan Cherki are being followed across the Pyrenees, notably by Real Madrid.
The club has also added Erling Haaland to its shortlist. Unsurprisingly, the Norwegian is expected to be City's most sought-after player should sanctions be imposed.
Haaland reportedly dreams of playing for Real Madrid. The club has followed him for a long time but opted to sign Kylian Mbappé two years ago. If Haaland were to become available, Los Blancos would be in the running. The same goes for FC Barcelona .
The Sun claims the Catalans are keeping a close eye on him, as they want to sign a center-forward after Robert Lewandowski 's departure and the failed pursuit of Julian Alvarez . We're not there yet, and officially, City hasn't received any sanctions.
But behind the scenes, clubs have already identified players to watch should the English side drop points or even be relegated. If that happens, teams looking to sign Manchester City players would still have to pay transfer fees.

Television Business Editor
The MTV Video Music Awards scored their largest audience in more than a decade on Sunday night.
The awards averaged 8.43 million viewers on CBS and MTV (including an encore on the latter), up by 51 percent from last year’s 5.6 million — which was also a multi-year high. Sunday’s audience (subject to adjustments when Nielsen adds its big data component) was the biggest for the VMAs since the 2015 show brought in more than 12 million people across multiple channels.
The VMAs also had their best performance among adults 18-49 (2.66 million in that age range) since 2018; among adults 25-54 (3.11 million) since 2019; and among adults 18-34 (1.09 million) since 2020.
Madonna — who also opened the show with a performance featuring Charli XCX and Sabrina Carpenter — was the night’s big winner with seven awards. Taylor Swift won video of the year for “The Fate of Ophelia” and also was given the first Artist Director award for musical artists who also direct videos.
The awards, hosted by Snoop Dogg, also featured tributes to Dolly Parton and George Michael. Nirvana was awarded the Video Vanguard honor.
The VMAs also benefited from what was likely a very large NFL lead-in. The awards peaked at 15 million viewers for Madonna’s opening number, which directly followed a game-winning field goal for the Baltimore Ravens over the Dallas Cowboys (who are perennially among the NFL’s biggest TV draws). The 2025 VMAs also had a strong NFL lead-in (23.9 million viewers), but the Ravens-Cowboys audience has a good chance of passing that mark.
CBS accounted for 7.61 million viewers, or 90 percent of the total audience. MTV’s simulcast drew 686,000 viewers, and the replay chipped in 142,000 more.
On social media, the awards accounted for 159 million video views across platforms, up 8 percent year to year.

articles.title_orig: Burnham offers Britain an 'honest conversation' on tackling problems
articles.title_zh: Burnham offers Britain an 'honest conversation' on tackling problems
articles.content_orig:
Conference speech day is always a big day for a prime minister, and perhaps no bigger than when it is your first one in the role.
The pitch from Andy Burnham is that "hope comes from honesty," there needs to be "less drift and more direction" and there needs to be a willingness to say "the things politicians usually avoid."
On Sunday, he told the BBC he wants to shake up social care in England , but would only be able to do so after a general election given he was committed to the tax promises Sir Keir Starmer made at the last general election.
This prompted a flurry of chat about how his social care plan could be paid for - and in particular the future of what is known as the triple lock, the promise to increase the state pension in line with wages, prices or 2.5%, whichever is the highest.
This was a policy introduced in 2010 by the Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition government to try to address pensioner poverty.
But plenty of politicians, in multiple parties, have long privately fretted that its cost is ballooning and will continue to do so, but would bemoan how politically difficult it would be to drop it.
It's a tricky one for the prime minister: he has the leader of the Unite union, Sharon Graham, saying it could be "electoral suicide" to ditch the triple lock.
Meanwhile the markets - which determine the cost of borrowing for the government - are keeping a keen eye on whether Burnham's promises appear to be financially credible.
In other words, he has to be able to point to things where money won't be spent, as well as where it will be.
No10 are being pretty coy about precisely what Andy Burnham will or won't say on all this later on.
They really don't want to overcook it or overdo it, instead suggesting it is others who have been getting carried away.
But ministers are well aware that a hare is running about it all - and given that, it would be extraordinary if there was no mention of it all, given that promise about "honesty," candour and trade offs.
Sufficiently extraordinary that his critics would pounce on what they'd see as a precise lack of the very thing he is promising - candour.
Folk I am hearing from this morning suggest, as one figure put it, "people will be surprised on the upside" about how much Burnham will be willing to lean into the options that could be explored as part of Labour's offer at the next general election.
He will be explicit it will be retained, as promised, until the election.
Instead, it would appear Burnham will seek to seed a conversation about all of the above, without nailing down the details.
His allies see this as a different approach to politics – being open about options, starting a debate but not crudely or abruptly shifting policy.
There is an implicit comparison with Sir Keir Starmer's ditching of the Winter Fuel Payment – which appeared to come from nowhere and had a near immediate impact.
But that didn't stop Graham likening the two approaches – claiming "the danger of doing it" is that Labour could "waste" a second hearing which it now has under Andy Burnham.
In the round, though, ministers I speak to are relishing what they see as a return to big arguments, about generational issues with a prime minister willing to wrestle with them in public.
This afternoon we will get a fuller sense of the scope and scale of that – on social care, pensions and much else.

articles.content_orig:
The new Bose Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds connect via USB-C and work with almost any device.
Bose wants to get back to basics, it seems – it just launched a new pair of wired earbuds with ANC , citing a rise in wired listening popularity. The earbuds connect to any USB-C device, using an internal, proprietary DSP to ensure they work in just about any USB-C port. With any source input, the earbuds output a fixed 24bit signal.
Bose is well-known for its Quiet Comfort lineup in recent years, but it didn’t start there. Still, the company can be considered one of the main players responsible for quality ANC in wireless headphones. After all, the QC35’s became the go-to travel option for some time.
This release, however, has literal strings attached. It needs USB-C to operate, not a 3.5mm output as most wired enthusiasts prefer at a minimum. That means you wouldn’t be able to use your own DAC/amp setup.
Even still, Bose’s Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds will be a good option for those who need ANC without the battery anxiety. Bose says the earbuds have two microphones on each bud to power active noise cancellation. Quiet Mode blocks most noise out, and Aware Mode acts as a transparency setting. ANC can also be disabled.
The new wired Bose earbuds are available to pre-order starting today for $99 in Black and White Smoke. Bose says the buds will begin shipping on October 15 for those who order from the official website and Best Buy.
